rationale.headline: T21 are clear favourites to beat T14, mostly on cleaner attacking play.

drivers.label: Breaking through the defence
drivers.detail: T21 completed line-breaking passes more reliably, slicing through T14's lines more often.

drivers.label: Converting chances
drivers.detail: T21 turned more of its forward runs into real scoring looks than T14 did.

drivers.label: Scoring vs leaking goals
drivers.detail: T21 created more and conceded less across the group stage, a stronger net goal balance.

drivers.label: Controlling the ball
drivers.detail: T21 held possession noticeably more, keeping T14 chasing the game.

rationale.methodNote: Market-blind: per-team penetration/creation profiles (line-break success, 4-unit penetration share, offer conversion, shrunk attack/defence rates, possession) are differenced (team A − team B) into one feature vector. Three one-vs-rest gradient-boosted regression ensembles (40 rounds, depth 3, learning rate 0.1), trained on leakage-safe group-stage rows (each match seen only with prior-match profiles), score the home/draw/away outcomes; scores are clamped to [0,1] and normalised to sum to 1. No betting odds, prices, or market-implied probabilities were used.
